mostWorthwhile.text: Making the collagen-rich extracellular matrix connected gene expression and protein production to material outside the cells, clarifying that tissue includes cells and their surroundings.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two branches followed a similar differentiation-then-amino-acid pattern, so the second protein-making combination felt somewhat repetitive, even though the different outcomes mattered.

surprise.text: The muscle precursors remained separate, single-nucleus cells containing actin and myosin rather than becoming mature fibres immediately.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary: the conditions, messages, amino acids and extracellular processing each had a stated purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the separate myoblasts develop into muscle and how the supporting matrix contributes to tissue structure.
